title: Learning from national reports and data
blurb: Use Ockenden, East Kent, MBRRACE-UK and Saving Babies' Lives v3 to explain what went wrong nationally and what midwives now do differently.
question: A midwife is planning postnatal care for a Black woman living in a deprived area. According to MBRRACE-UK 2022–24, how does her risk of dying during or after pregnancy compare with a White woman's?

teach.body: SPM 1.4 asks midwives to identify, critically analyse and interpret local, national and international data and reports; SPM 1.5 to use and share their lessons to inform practice and support women's evidence-informed decisions; SPM 4.2 to use data on prevalence and risk. In plain English: the big reports tell you where women and babies were harmed, and who is most at risk, so you can recognise the same patterns on your own shift.

teach.caption: Ockenden's actions apply to all maternity services in England.
Examples: staff who work together must train together; plain-language investigation reports for families.

teach.h: East Kent: four areas for action
teach.body: Reading the signals found that warning signs were missed and families were not listened to. Its four areas for action are: identifying poorly performing units; giving care with compassion and kindness; teamworking with a common purpose; and responding to challenge with honesty. For a midwife on shift, that means listening to women, working as one team with obstetricians and neonatologists, and being honest when things go wrong.

teach.h: Saving Babies' Lives v3: six elements
teach.caption: Part of the national ambition to halve perinatal mortality from 2010 to 2025.

teach.body: Abena, a Black woman from one of the most deprived areas, had a caesarean and has a history of anxiety. Midwife Claire uses MBRRACE-UK: thromboembolism is the leading cause of death up to 6 weeks, so she checks Abena's VTE risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis; suicide is the leading cause from 6 weeks to a year, so she asks about her mood and makes sure the GP and health visitor know her history. She also listens carefully to any symptom Abena reports.
teach.cite: MBRRACE-UK data brief 2022–24; East Kent area 2

teach.text: Two different time windows: thrombosis and thromboembolism lead during pregnancy and up to 6 weeks after; maternal suicide leads from 6 weeks to 1 year. And the disparity is nearly three times for Black women, while deprivation doubles the rate.

items: Ockenden (March 2022): 15 immediate and essential actions, e.g. staff who work together must train together.
East Kent (October 2022): identify poor units, compassion and kindness, common purpose, honesty under challenge.
MBRRACE-UK 2022–24: 12.80 per 100,000; thromboembolism leads to 6 weeks, suicide from 6 weeks to 1 year.
Black women nearly three times the rate of White women; most deprived areas twice the least deprived.
SBL v3 elements: smoking, growth, movements, fetal monitoring, preterm birth, diabetes.

summary: You can now name what Ockenden, East Kent, MBRRACE-UK and Saving Babies' Lives v3 found or require. You can also turn their data on causes and inequalities into specific actions for the women you care for.

A.q: How many immediate and essential actions did the final Ockenden report set for maternity services?
A.why: The Ockenden final report (30 March 2022) set 15 immediate and essential actions for all English trusts.

whyNot.0: Four is the number of areas for action in the East Kent report.
whyNot.1: Seven is not the number of Ockenden actions.
whyNot.2: Twelve is not the number of Ockenden actions.

A.q: According to MBRRACE-UK 2022–24, what was the leading cause of maternal death during pregnancy or up to 6 weeks after?
A.why: Thrombosis and thromboembolism were the leading cause during or up to 6 weeks after pregnancy, followed by cardiac disease and psychiatric causes.

whyNot.1: Haemorrhage was not the leading cause in 2022–24.
whyNot.2: Sepsis was not the leading cause in 2022–24.
whyNot.3: Hypertensive disorders were not the leading cause in 2022–24.

A.q: Which of these is an element of Saving Babies' Lives version 3?
options: Raising awareness of reduced fetal movement
A.why: SBL v3 element 3 is raising awareness of reduced fetal movement. The others are smoking, fetal growth, fetal monitoring in labour, preterm birth and pre-existing diabetes.

whyNot.0: Caesarean rates are not an SBL v3 element.
whyNot.2: Home birth rates are not an SBL v3 element.
whyNot.3: There is no universal GBS screening in the UK, and it is not an SBL v3 element.

B.q: A woman at 5 months postnatal is low in mood. Which MBRRACE-UK 2022–24 finding should guide the midwife's or health visitor's response?
options: Cardiac disease is the leading cause after 6 weeks
Psychiatric deaths are rare after the birth
Maternal suicide leads from 6 weeks to 1 year
Most deaths after 6 weeks are from sepsis
B.why: Maternal suicide was the leading cause of death from 6 weeks to 1 year after pregnancy; psychiatric causes accounted for 33% of these late maternal deaths.

whyNot.0: Cardiac disease was second during pregnancy and up to 6 weeks; suicide leads after 6 weeks.
whyNot.1: Psychiatric causes accounted for a third of late maternal deaths (6 weeks to 1 year).
whyNot.3: Sepsis is not the leading cause after 6 weeks.

B.q: Which of these is one of the four areas for action in the East Kent report Reading the signals?
B.why: The four areas are identifying poorly performing units, giving care with compassion and kindness, teamworking with a common purpose, and responding to challenge with honesty.

whyNot.1: Continuity of carer is not one of the four areas.
whyNot.2: Induction rates are not one of the four areas.
whyNot.3: Building birth centres is not one of the four areas.

B.q: According to MBRRACE-UK 2022–24, how did maternal mortality for women in the most deprived areas compare with the least deprived?
B.why: In England, women in the most deprived areas had twice the mortality of those in the least deprived.

whyNot.0: There was a clear gap, not equal rates.
whyNot.2: Nearly three times is the disparity for Black women compared with White women.
whyNot.3: Five times is not the 2022–24 figure.

C.q: A Black woman, aged 37, who had a caesarean 4 days ago calls the community midwife with a painful, swollen left calf. Which response best applies the national data?
options: Advise rest and review at the next visit
Suggest she contacts her GP next week
C.why: Thromboembolism is the leading cause of maternal death up to 6 weeks; she has VTE risk factors (caesarean birth, age over 35), and Black women had nearly three times the maternal mortality rate of White women. Suspected VTE needs urgent same-day assessment.

whyNot.1: A week's delay is unsafe for suspected VTE.
whyNot.3: Self-care advice does not assess or treat a suspected DVT.

C.q: A labour ward plans its emergency training after reading Ockenden. Which plan best fits the report?
options: Separate drills for midwives and doctors
Multidisciplinary drills with the whole team
Training for band 7 midwives to cascade
C.why: Ockenden action 7: staff who work together must train together, so multidisciplinary drills are the fit.

whyNot.0: Separate drills do not build teamwork across professions.
whyNot.1: E-learning alone does not rehearse teamwork.
whyNot.3: Cascading does not give every team member shared practice.

C.q: A midwife is preparing a teaching session on MBRRACE-UK 2022–24. Which statement is accurate?
options: Black women had twice the White rate
Age 35 and over carried lower risk
C.why: 252 direct and indirect deaths among 1,969,321 maternities gave 12.80 per 100,000, 20% higher than 2009–11.

whyNot.1: The rate was 20% higher than 2009–11, not lower.
whyNot.2: Black women had nearly three times the rate; twice is the deprivation gap.
whyNot.3: Women aged 35 and over were at higher risk.

reteach.title: Turning reports into actions
reteach.question: What does each national source change on your shift?

blocks.body: Ockenden: train with the whole team and escalate staffing concerns. East Kent: listen, be kind, work to a common purpose, be honest. MBRRACE-UK: think VTE early after birth, ask about mood after 6 weeks, and recognise higher risk for Black women, deprived areas and age 35+. SBL v3: smoking, growth, movements, fetal monitoring, preterm birth and diabetes care.

blocks.text: Fifteen actions is Ockenden; four areas is East Kent. Do not swap them.

explain.body: The final report of the review of Shrewsbury and Telford maternity services (30 March 2022) grew from 23 families to nearly 1,500 and set 15 immediate and essential actions for all trusts in England.

test.q: Which maternity service was the subject of the Ockenden review?
test.why: The Ockenden review examined maternity care at Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust.

whyNot.0: East Kent was the subject of Reading the signals.
whyNot.1: Morecambe Bay was an earlier, separate investigation.
whyNot.2: Cwm Taf Morgannwg in Wales was reviewed separately.

explain.body: MBRRACE-UK 2022–24 (England data): Black women had nearly three times the maternal mortality rate of White women; the most deprived areas had twice the rate of the least deprived.

items.label: Reference: White women or least deprived

test.q: According to MBRRACE-UK 2022–24, how did the maternal mortality rate for Black women compare with White women?
options: About one and a half times
test.why: In England, Black women had nearly three times the maternal mortality rate of White women.

whyNot.1: The gap was larger than one and a half times.
whyNot.2: Twice is the deprivation gap, not the ethnicity gap.

explain.body: Element 1 smoking (CO testing at booking and 36 weeks), element 2 growth, element 3 reduced movements, element 4 fetal monitoring (fresh eyes), element 5 preterm birth, element 6 pre-existing diabetes.

test.q: Hourly fresh eyes review of a CTG belongs to which Saving Babies' Lives v3 element?
test.why: Element 4, effective fetal monitoring during labour, includes fresh eyes reviews and annual competency assessment.

whyNot.0: Element 2 covers growth surveillance, not intrapartum monitoring.
whyNot.2: Element 3 covers awareness and management of reduced movements.
whyNot.3: Element 5 covers preterm birth and perinatal optimisation.

explain.body: SPM 1.4: critically analyse and interpret data. MBRRACE-UK figures are rates per 100,000 maternities with confidence intervals; compare like periods and note what is included (direct and indirect deaths).

test.q: MBRRACE-UK reports 252 maternal deaths among 1,969,321 maternities in 2022–24. How is the rate expressed?
test.why: 252 divided by 1,969,321, multiplied by 100,000, gives 12.80 per 100,000 maternities.

whyNot.1: Per 10,000 the figure would be about 1.28, not 12.80.
whyNot.2: Per 1,000 the figure would be about 0.128.
whyNot.3: 252 is the number of deaths, not a rate of 2.52 per 100,000.
